content: The initial recommended dose of lipase is 500 units per kilogram of body weight per meal, with adjustments made up to the maximum allowable dose. For snacks, half of the prescribed dose for a full meal is typically administered. The total daily dose should account for approximately three meals and two to three snacks. The dose should not exceed 2,500 lipase units per kilogram per meal, 10,000 lipase units per kilogram per day, or 4,000 lipase units per gram of fat consumed daily. For patients using Creon, a dose of 72,000 lipase units per meal is recommended when consuming at least 100 grams of fat per day. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, diarrhea, abdominal cramping, headache, neck pain, nasal congestion, peripheral edema, rash, dizziness, hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, exacerbation of diabetes mellitus, flatulence, dyspepsia, biliary tract stones, abnormal stools, hydrocholecystis, renal cysts, viral infections, asthma, gastritis, and muscle spasms. Serious adverse effects, such as hypersensitivity to any component of the medication or acute pancreatitis (including acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis), have been reported. Fibrosing colonopathy, which can progress to colonic strictures, has also been documented. The medication’s dosage depends on the specific condition being treated and the patient’s digestive requirements. The contents of the capsules should not be administered alone or mixed with food, as this may cause irritation of the oral mucosa or reduce enzyme activity. During pregnancy, this medication is classified as Category C, meaning it should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether the drug passes into breast milk, so caution is advised during lactation. This medication contains digestive enzymes that are naturally required by the body to break down and digest food. It is used when the pancreas is unable to produce or release sufficient digestive enzymes into the gastrointestinal tract. Some supplement products may contain harmful impurities or additives, and the FDA has not reviewed this product for safety or efficacy. If using the tablet form, avoid keeping it in the mouth, as this can irritate the gums and cheeks. Swallow the medication with water, and do not change brands or dosage forms without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. If a dose is missed, take the next dose with your next meal or snack as directed. Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
